posts.topic: The worst listing of the week
posts.why: Closes the local week on its most concrete artefact.

tiktok.hook: The worst listing I found this week is marked permanently closed. It is open.
beats: Somebody has been losing customers since January
tiktok.vo: The worst listing I found this week is marked permanently closed on Google, and the shop is open every single day. It has been like that for about eleven months, which means every person who searched for it found a business that had died, and there was nobody to tell them otherwise. A closed listing is not a small mistake. It is an eleven month outage nobody noticed.
tiktok.cap: Marked permanently closed. Open every day. For eleven months.
tiktok.body: The shop is open daily. Google has said permanently closed for about eleven months. Every search found a dead business, and nobody was told otherwise. A closed listing is not a small mistake, it is an outage.

instagram.cap: Check your own status tonight. One wrong field, eleven months of silence.
instagram.body: Wrong hours, wrong number, wrong status — these fields are set once and never looked at again, which is exactly why they fail quietly for a year.

facebook.body:
The worst listing I found this week is marked 'permanently closed' on Google. The shop is open every single day.

It has been like that for about eleven months.

Every person who searched for it found a business that had died, and there was nobody to tell them otherwise.

That is not a small mistake. It is an eleven-month outage nobody noticed.

Go and check yours right now.

posts.why: The third honest ledger, and it is the one that builds the habit.

tiktok.hook: Three weeks in. Here is the number, honestly, including what did not work.
tiktok.vo: Three weeks in, read off the tracker. The teardowns travel furthest, the checklists get saved, and the honest ads convert but do not travel at all, which is exactly what the plan predicted and still feels wrong when it happens. Nothing here is a promise. It is a record of one account for twenty one days, and it is the only kind of number I trust.
tiktok.cap: Teardowns travel. Checklists get saved. Honest ads convert and do not travel.
tiktok.body: Three weeks, read off the tracker: teardowns travel furthest, checklists get saved, honest ads convert but do not travel at all. That matches the plan and still feels wrong when it happens.

instagram.cap: Three different jobs, three different shapes. Stop judging them all by views.
instagram.body: Posting eleven things a day only makes sense if you expect them to do different jobs. Judging a sell post by its views is a category error, and it will make you stop selling.

facebook.body:
Three weeks in, read off the tracker rather than my memory.

Teardowns travel furthest. Checklists get saved. Honest ads convert but barely travel at all.

That last one is what the plan predicted, and it still feels wrong when it happens.

Nothing here is a promise. It is a record of one account for twenty-one days, which is the only kind of number I trust.

What is your own tracker saying?

posts.why: Shows the format is a system, not a lucky post.

tiktok.hook: The most shared thing I posted this week was a teardown. Here is the format, on a new business.
tiktok.vo: The most shared post of the week was a teardown, so here is the format on a new business. Show the page. Name one problem in a single sentence. Give three fixes that take under an hour. Leave out the insults entirely, because the moment it becomes a joke at their expense it stops being useful and starts being content.
tiktok.cap: Show it. One problem. Three fixes. No insults. That is the whole format.
tiktok.body: Show the page, name one problem in one sentence, give three fixes under an hour each, and leave out the mockery. Shared because it was useful, not because it was cruel.

instagram.cap: The format works because it is generous. Keep it that way.
instagram.body: A teardown that makes the owner laugh with you gets shared by them. One that makes them the joke gets shared by strangers and lost forever.

facebook.body:
The format, since it is the most shared thing I post:

1. Show the page.
2. Name one problem, in one sentence.
3. Give three fixes, each under an hour.
4. No insults.

The moment it becomes a joke at the owner's expense it stops being useful and starts being content.

Send me a link and I will run it on yours.

posts.why: Good news for small businesses, which makes it shareable.

tiktok.hook: Lagos rewards whoever answers, not whoever is best.
beats: That is a small business advantage
tiktok.vo: Lagos rewards whoever answers, not whoever is best, which is genuinely good news if you are small. You cannot outspend the big shop, but you can reply in eleven minutes at nine at night, and in this market that is a bigger competitive advantage than a better logo, because almost nobody does it consistently.
tiktok.cap: You cannot outspend them. You can out-reply them.
tiktok.body: Lagos rewards whoever answers, not whoever is best. You cannot outspend the big shop, but you can reply in eleven minutes at nine at night, and almost nobody does it consistently.

instagram.cap: The fastest reply in the market is a marketing strategy.
instagram.body: Reply speed is the one advantage that costs nothing, needs no budget, and cannot be bought by a competitor with more money than you.

facebook.body:
Lagos rewards whoever answers, not whoever is best.

Which is good news if you are small. You cannot outspend the big shop, but you can reply in eleven minutes at nine at night — and almost nobody does that consistently.

It costs nothing, needs no budget, and cannot be bought by a competitor with more money.

How fast do you reply?

posts.why: Audience action is the only real proof of reach.

tiktok.hook: Someone watched one of these videos and fixed their Google listing that night.
tiktok.vo: Someone watched the listing video, commented that hers was empty, and fixed it that night. Two hours later she sent a screenshot: photos, hours, the right number, a category. I do not know whether it brought her customers, and I am not going to pretend I do. What I know is that a video changed something real in a real business within two hours, which is rarer than a viral post.
tiktok.cap: She fixed her listing two hours after watching. That is the only proof that matters.
tiktok.body: Someone watched the listing video, fixed hers that night, and sent a screenshot: photos, hours, right number, category. I do not know if it brought customers. I know it changed something real within two hours.

instagram.cap: One real action beats a thousand views you cannot verify.
instagram.body: Reach is a number. One person changing something in their business two hours later is a result, and it is worth more than a screenshot of views.

facebook.body:
Someone watched the listing video, commented that hers was empty, and fixed it that night.

Two hours later she sent a screenshot: photos, hours, the right number, a category.

I do not know whether it brought her customers, and I will not pretend I do. But a video changed something real in a real business within two hours — which is rarer than a viral post.

What did you fix after watching something?

posts.why: A ranked answer is more useful than a list.

tiktok.hook: If I had one hour in any Lagos business, I would fix two things: reply time, then the first sentence.
tiktok.vo: If I had one hour in any Lagos business, I would fix two things and ignore everything else. First, reply time, because a good reply at the wrong speed is a lost customer. Second, the first sentence on the homepage, because it is doing more work than the rest of the page combined. The logo can wait forever. It has waited this long already.
tiktok.cap: Reply time first. First sentence second. Everything else can wait.
tiktok.body: One hour, two fixes: reply time, then the first sentence on the homepage. A good reply at the wrong speed is a lost customer, and the first sentence is doing more work than the rest of the page combined.

instagram.cap: The logo can wait. It has waited this long already.
instagram.body: Order matters because attention is finite. Fixing the reply changes every conversation this week; fixing the logo changes how you feel about the page.

facebook.body:
If I had one hour in any Lagos business, I would fix two things and ignore everything else.

1. Reply time. A good reply at the wrong speed is a lost customer.
2. The first sentence on the homepage. It does more work than the rest of the page combined.

The logo can wait forever. It has waited this long already.

What would your two be?

posts.why: Publishing the flop keeps the receipts series honest.

tiktok.hook: The post that flopped hardest this week was the one I liked most.
tiktok.vo: The post that flopped hardest this week was the one I liked most. It was about measurement, it opened with a definition, and there was no image until the third second. I liked it because it was clever, and it flopped because clever is not a reason to keep watching. I am showing it to you so I stop doing this.
tiktok.cap: It flopped because it was clever, and clever is not a reason to keep watching.
tiktok.body: The one I liked most flopped hardest. It opened with a definition and had no image until second three. Clever is not a reason to keep watching, which is a lesson I apparently need monthly.

instagram.cap: Favourite is not the same as good, and definitely not the same as watched.
instagram.body: Your favourite post is usually the one where you pleased yourself. The audience can tell, and it is not unkind about it, it just scrolls.

facebook.body:
The post that flopped hardest this week was the one I liked most.

It was about measurement. It opened with a definition. There was no image until the third second.

I liked it because it was clever. It flopped because clever is not a reason to keep watching.

I am showing it to you so I stop doing this.

What is the last thing you liked and nobody else did?

posts.why: A number so low it becomes a call to action by itself.

tiktok.hook: I asked twelve businesses if they had claimed their Google listing. Two had.
beats: Both were the ones with staff
The other ten did not know it was free
tiktok.vo: I asked twelve businesses on one street whether they had claimed their Google listing. Two had. Both of those had somebody whose job included it, and the other ten did not know it was free, which is the part I keep coming back to. It is free. It takes an hour. And ten of twelve had not done it.
tiktok.cap: Two of twelve. The other ten did not know it was free.
tiktok.body: Twelve businesses on one street. Two had claimed their listing. The other ten did not know it was free, which is the part I keep coming back to.

instagram.cap: An hour of work your ten nearest competitors have not done.
instagram.body: The reason to do it tonight is not that it is clever. It is that almost nobody around you has, and the gap closes when a video like this reaches them.

facebook.body:
I asked twelve businesses on one street whether they had claimed their Google listing.

Two had.

The other ten did not know it was free.

It is free. It takes about an hour. And ten of your twelve nearest competitors have not done it.

If you are one of the ten, tonight is a good night.

posts.why: One line, one code, exactly as the format prescribes.

tiktok.hook: Most requested this week: the free review. Three points, twenty-four hours, no pitch.
tiktok.vo: Most requested this week was not a pack, it was the free review. Send a link, get three points in twenty four hours, no call, no pitch, no obligation. If you want the whole method rather than three points, the packs start at five thousand naira, and I will tell you which one is wrong for you if it is wrong for you.
tiktok.cap: Free review: three points in 24 hours, no pitch. WhatsApp: 0905 069 0837.
tiktok.body: Most requested this week was the free review, not a pack. Send a link, get three points in twenty-four hours, no call and no pitch. The packs start at five thousand if you want the whole method.

instagram.cap: Free is the easiest thing to say yes to, and it demonstrates the work.
instagram.body: Three specific points in writing beat a sales call and a brochure. It also tells both of us whether the paid work would be useful.

facebook.body:
Most requested this week was not a pack. It was the free review.

Send your link, get three points in 24 hours. No call. No pitch. No obligation to reply.

If you want the whole method rather than three points, the packs start at ₦5,000 — and I will tell you if the one you are looking at is wrong for you.

WhatsApp: 0905 069 0837.

posts.why: A refusal that states a principle rather than a mood.

tiktok.hook: We declined a brief this week. It was to make a business sound bigger than it is.
beats: Then they have to maintain it
tiktok.vo: We declined a brief this week to make a one person business look like a fifteen person agency: a team page with stock portraits, an address in a building they do not work in, and award logos they had not won. Not because it is illegal, but because the first client who asks to visit would end the relationship, and they would have built a website that only works if nobody looks closely.
tiktok.cap: A website that only works if nobody looks closely is not a website.
tiktok.body: Stock team portraits, an address they do not work at, awards they have not won. Legal, briefly effective, and it collapses the first time a client asks to visit. We declined.

instagram.cap: Credibility built on a lie expires the first time someone checks.
instagram.body: Being one person is a selling point if you say it plainly, because it means the person answering is the person doing the work.

facebook.body:
We declined a brief this week: make a one-person business look like a fifteen-person agency.

Stock team portraits. An address in a building they do not work in. Award logos they had not won.

Not illegal. But the first client who asks to visit ends the relationship, and they would have a website that only works if nobody looks closely.

Have you ever been sold a team that did not exist?

posts.why: Sets up the sell week without apologising for it.

tiktok.hook: Next week is everything we sell, and who should not buy it.
tiktok.vo: Next week I am going to show you everything we sell, with prices, and who should not buy each one. That is unusual for an account that spends most of its time entertaining people, and it is the point of the month: you spend three weeks being useful and then you tell people what you make, once, plainly, so nobody has to guess.
tiktok.cap: Next week: all nine packs, all prices, and who should not buy each one.
tiktok.body: Three weeks of being useful, then one week of saying plainly what we sell and who should not buy it. Nobody has to guess, and nobody has to be sold to.

slides: And who should not buy it
instagram.cap: One honest selling week beats a month of hints.
instagram.body: Hints are worse than prices. A price lets someone decide, and a decision is better for both of us than a vague hope.

facebook.body:
Next week I am going to show you everything we sell, with prices, and who should not buy each one.

That is unusual for an account that mostly entertains people, and it is the whole point of the month: spend three weeks being useful, then say plainly what you make, once, so nobody has to guess.

Hints are worse than prices. A price lets someone decide.

What would you want to see first?
